title: These 12 Mistakes Make Your App Feel CHEAP
access_checked: Watch metadata, description, and rendered English captions checked
takeaway: Primary source for the twelve spoken topics in order and the Mobbin promotion.
limitations: Untimed caption renders; audio and visuals not independently verified. Creator opinions and commercial examples are not independent outcome evidence.

title: View video transcripts
takeaway: In a captioned video description, Show transcript opens the publisher’s transcript and selecting a line seeks to that point.
limitations: Availability can vary with the watch surface and caption availability.

title: Vamo
takeaway: Creator-authored illustrations of a verification wait, route pay, progress, and next steps.
limitations: Not a test of the featured video’s claims. Does not isolate any intervention; do not copy the described artificial wait.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
access_checked: Public Recommendation and selected Understanding pages checked
takeaway: Use specific success criteria for labels, errors, status, repeated entry, focus, targets, resize, and reflow. See the criterion map below.
limitations: WCAG conformance is scoped to content and complete processes, and requires more than these selected checks. The Understanding pages are explanatory. Verify the target’s legal and platform scope.

title: Functional Images
takeaway: Alternatives for functional images describe the action or destination; redundant decorative images need not be read twice.
limitations: Examples are web implementations, not a native API contract or a study of icon style.

title: Involving Users in Evaluating Web Accessibility
takeaway: Involve users with disabilities in usability evaluation alongside technical conformance checks.
limitations: A small sample or one assistive technology does not represent all users or prove conformance.

title: Privacy — Human Interface Guidelines
takeaway: Ask in context for necessary access, use purpose copy, and respect a choice not to grant it.
limitations: Apple design guidance; prompt behavior and availability vary by capability/OS. Check current policy separately.

title: Request runtime permissions
takeaway: Ask in context, check permission as needed, and degrade gracefully on denial; there are OS-managed mechanisms and alternatives.
limitations: Relevant permission type and API version matter. Not a Play policy or consent substitute.

title: Progress indicators — Human Interface Guidelines
takeaway: Use a determinate indicator for measurable work, an indeterminate one when duration/work is unknown, and concise status context.
limitations: No app-wide threshold or evidence that more animation improves outcomes. Pause/cancel must match capability.

title: SF Symbols
takeaway: A library with consistent weight/scale and directional or localized variants illustrates how a family supports a design system.
limitations: An Apple library example, not a test of matching strokes or a mandate to replace other platform icons.

title: Typography — Human Interface Guidelines
takeaway: Built-in text styles support scalable text and legible hierarchy; adapt to larger accessibility sizes.
limitations: Apple guidance, not a universal web zoom requirement. Check actual layout and supported native settings.

title: Test your app with pseudolocales
takeaway: Android’s expansion and bidirectional pseudo locales can reveal hardcoded strings, clipping, and layout issues before translation.
limitations: Pseudolocales do not check translation quality or replace tests in real supported locales.

title: App Review Guidelines — Privacy (§5.1)
access_checked: Public policy, including §5.1.1 privacy-policy text, checked
takeaway: Apple specifies accessible in-app and listing privacy policy links and rules for data collection and storage under its review guidelines.
limitations: Platform distribution requirements, not a global rule or an assurance of App Review approval. Recheck current text.

title: User Data — Prominent Disclosure & Consent Requirement
access_checked: Full-policy section on prominent disclosure/consent checked
takeaway: For covered data access, collection, use, or sharing outside reasonable expectations, Play requires prominent in-app disclosure and affirmative consent, with sequencing rules.
limitations: Apply the policy scope and feature-specific rules; neither the system prompt nor placing text in the privacy policy alone substitutes for it.

title: Berman v. Freedom Financial Network, LLC, 30 F.4th 849
author_or_organization: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
access_checked: Relevant sections of court opinion accessed
takeaway: The opinion distinguishes conspicuous notice of terms and an action that unambiguously manifests assent in the cases before it.
limitations: Specific jurisdiction and facts, not a universal design recipe or psychological evidence of trust.

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR)
author_or_organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
access_checked: Public official text; relevant article excerpts checked
takeaway: Check scope (Art. 3), minimization (Art. 5), lawful basis (Art. 6), consent conditions when used (Art. 7), and transparency obligations (Arts. 12–14).
limitations: Does not apply to every project; lawfulness and consent validity require contextual review. A privacy notice and consent are different.

title: Bringing Dark Patterns to Light
access_checked: Official report landing and PDF intro/examples checked
takeaway: Documents consumer harms from obscured key terms, confusing choices and difficult cancellation, with examples and recommendations.
limitations: Staff report in a U.S. regulatory context, not a binding rule by itself or a universal numerical estimate.

title: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
takeaway: Status visibility, control/escape, consistency, recognition over recall, and recovery are useful audit prompts.
limitations: Heuristics—not normative standards or a quantitative estimate of each intervention.

title: Designing Empty States in Complex Applications: 3 Guidelines
takeaway: Distinguish causes, communicate state, and give useful starting or recovery actions where appropriate.
limitations: Complex-app examples, not a controlled estimate or a rule that every empty state needs a CTA.

title: Text input — Hint text
access_checked: Public hint section and example checked
takeaway: Use a short, relevant hint on format/use, attached to a persistent input label and field association.
limitations: Style conventions are service-specific. Long explanations or material disclosures belong in an appropriate visible format.

title: Confirmation pages
takeaway: After a transaction, give a reference if available, clear next steps, and a record users can revisit or save.
limitations: Pattern for public transactions; adapt to the action’s stakes. Does not prove that the receiving process has finished.

title: Error message
takeaway: Explain what to fix inline and in a linked summary where appropriate; preserve responses. Keep service problems separate from invalid input.
limitations: Service-specific pattern. Preserve only data safe to keep; security can require less specific messages.

title: Button
takeaway: Describe the button’s action or consequence. Continue and Save and continue differ if information is saved.
limitations: Examples and conventions, not an experiment or a reason to overwrite appropriate local terminology.

title: Filtering
takeaway: Match batch/instant behavior to the use case; indicate applied filters, provide removal or reset, and define defaults.
limitations: A design pattern, not an effect size; application-owned constraints and state must be handled separately.

source_type: industry usability observations and benchmark examples
title: Display “Applied Filters” in an Overview (28% Don’t)
takeaway: An overview of applied filters supports confirmation, removal, and context on mobile and desktop e-commerce lists.
limitations: Benchmarked site prevalence is not user uplift. Public article summarizes research; not a randomized test on all app types.

title: The Psychology of Waiting Lines
takeaway: Proposes that uncertainty and lack of explanation can make waits more difficult for service customers.
limitations: A management essay with propositions, not a controlled app or spinner study. Do not attribute it to the video as its unnamed source.

title: What to tell consumers in waits of different lengths: An integrative model of service evaluation
author_or_organization: M. K. Hui & D. K. Tse
access_checked: Institutional abstract checked; no full-text file in the repository
takeaway: The roles of waiting-duration and queue information varied with wait length. Acceptability and affect mediated service evaluation; perceived duration did not in their model.
limitations: Abstract-level inference; service wait conditions, not a modern app spinner or a rule for a fixed number of seconds.

title: The effect of skeleton screens
takeaway: In one fictional news site, skeleton and spinner averages favored different outcomes and reported differences were not statistically significant.
limitations: One context and abstract-level conclusion. A null result does not prove equivalence or a universal winner.

title: Rethinking the Progress Bar
author_or_organization: C. Harrison, B. Amento, S. Kuznetsov & R. Bell
access_checked: Public author-hosted paper and method checked
takeaway: Participants compared progress bars with different progress profiles but equal 5.5-second duration. Appearance can affect perceived wait independent of elapsed time.
limitations: Artificial task and fixed duration; not evidence to fake progress, slow the app, or predict conversion.

title: Measuring symbol and icon characteristics: Norms for concreteness, complexity, meaningfulness, familiarity, and semantic distance for 239 symbols
author_or_organization: S. J. P. McDougall, M. B. Curry & O. de Bruijn
access_checked: Publisher metadata and abstract checked; paper PDF publicly linked
takeaway: Distinguishes several icon characteristics that can be evaluated, including familiarity, meaningfulness and distance from a referent.
limitations: Not a recommendation to use one icon library, or an estimate for stroke uniformity or today’s UI icons.

title: Android Permissions Remystified: A Field Study on Contextual Integrity
access_checked: Public proceedings page and paper available; study description checked
takeaway: In a 36-person field study, some protected-resource accesses were inconsistent with what participants expected or wanted.
limitations: Small sample and older Android permission model. Reported desires do not estimate the effect of a current OS prompt timing change.

title: Authentication Cheat Sheet — Authentication Responses
access_checked: Authentication responses and re-authentication guidance checked
takeaway: Authentication and recovery responses should avoid disclosing account existence/status; retain re-authentication policies for sensitive actions.
limitations: Does not disallow specific corrections for routine, safe field validation. Requires flow-specific security review.

title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
access_checked: Public article checked for retry risk and idempotency
takeaway: A timed-out write can have committed; model caller intent, operation identity, side effects, and late requests to retry safely.
limitations: Engineering pattern using AWS examples, not an automatic exactly-once guarantee or a replacement for provider-specific contracts.

title: Using moderated usability testing
author_or_organization: GOV.UK Service Manual user research community
takeaway: Recruit likely users, give believable neutral tasks, observe behavior, and plan assistive-technology participation and safe data handling.
limitations: Qualitative usability sessions surface issues but do not by themselves quantify a population effect.
